newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - ALUMINIUM TO CONSOLIDATE, COPPER TIRED.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - ALUMINIUM TO CONSOLIDATE, COPPER TIRED.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Aluminium may need to pause for a time as the market is still in overbought territory after its recent upswing, although longer term prices are still seen trending higher, technical analysts said.
Copper prices look to have run out of steam on the upside and a test of chart support at $2,270 may be forthcoming.

COPPER - Persistant increases in LME stocks and a narrower cash/threes backwardation continues to dampen sentiment in the copper market, which looks likely to take another look at the downside, analysts said.

"With the market running out of steam on the upside the $2,270 support level looks likely to be more seriously tested. Failure at this level would then bring the $2,250 and $2,226 levels into play," brokers Brandeis said in a commentary.
Three months copper was last indicated at $2,276/$2,280, which was just higher than Monday's kerb close of $2,274 but off from slightly firmer late trading levels.
ALUMINIUM - Sideways trading in the $1,730-$1,775 area is seen probable, although a break to the downside could spell bigger losses.
The 14-day RSI was still above 70, indicating that the market remained in overbought territory and was likely to consolidate or correct slightly lower before heading higher, analysts said.

"With the spread staying firm, trading above $10 back and another encouraging stock drawdown, aluminium's potential remains firmly on the upside," Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff said of the previous day's trading.
However, important support lurked not far below.

"This market could be consolidating before breaking higher again. However, $1,730 is very important support and if broken falls to $1,709 and lower could be seen," said Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading Ltd.
Three months aluminium was last quoted at $1,736/$1,740, versus $1,750 at Monday's kerb close.
